conclusion: A length-only fragment metric misses compact closed islands and long overlapping return contours. Organic interfaces use occupied footprint, real downstream extrusion demand and single-road planning for narrow contours. Physical minimum-width checks must follow overlap-height modulation so valid reduced-height contacts survive. Narrow rescue supports genuinely unfilled sub-line-width source strips without accepting final beads narrower than their physical height. True contacts, native trunks, Brim and actual model-surface gaps remain protected. Current test2 Release has no collapsed return contour, no self-intersecting closed interface route and no subheight interface bead; all retained short interface finishes support actual upper roads. Source-bound repeated Release exports, full native regressions and geometry checks support these claims.
scope: Reviewed native interface manufacturing and test2 Release output as of 2026-10-26; older evidence retains its original anchors.
